title: Medical Imaging Salary: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual, Fortnightly, and Fortnightly Pay
description: Learn how to calculate a medical imaging salary from an hourly rate using a 38-hour week, 52-week year. Includes award rates, casual loading, tax, and super from Fair Work Ombudsma
salarySummary: Medical imaging professionals earn a median full-time weekly earnings of $2,360 per 38-hour week, based on ABS data. Use hourly × 38 × 52 for annual, then divide by 26 for fortnightly.

faqs.q: What is the median weekly earnings for medical imaging professionals?
faqs.a: According to Jobs and Skills Australia, the median full-time weekly earnings for Medical Imaging Professionals (including medical diagnostic radiographers, sonographers, etc.) is $2,360 per week before tax, based on a 38-hour week. This is from the ABS Survey of Employee Earnings and Hours, May 2025. Casual rates are higher with 25% loading.

faqs.q: How do I calculate annual salary from an hourly rate for a medical imaging role?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by 38 hours per week, then by 52 weeks. For example, $60 per hour × 38 = $2,280 per week, then $2,280 × 52 = $118,560 annual. For a casual, add 25% loading on top (e.g., $75 per hour including loading). Super is 12% paid on top.

faqs.q: What award covers medical imaging professionals?
faqs.a: Medical imaging professionals are covered by the Health Professionals and Support Services Award or the Medical Practitioners Award. Minimum rates are set by the Fair Work Commission and updated annually. Pay guides from Fair Work Ombudsman provide exact rates. Always check the award for your classification.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Calculate a Medical Imaging Salary from an Hourly Rate

When you're looking at a **medical imaging salary**, you'll often see an hourly rate. To convert it to annual, annual, or fortnightly, use the simple formula: **hourly × hours per week × 52. This site assumes a **38-hour week** (the standard full-time ordinary hours. For a fortnight, multiply weekly pay by 2.

### The 38-Hour Week and the Fortnight

Most full-time medical imaging professionals work 38 hours per week, according to the ABS data from Jobs and Skills Australia. The median weekly earnings for Medical Imaging Professionals is **$2,360** per week before tax. That's based on a 38-hour week. If you're paid hourly, your weekly pay is rate × 38. Your fortnightly pay is weekly × 2.

### Award Rates and the National Minimum Wage

The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees get 25% loading: $33.05 per hour. But medical imaging professionals are covered by awards like the **Health Professionals and Support Services Award** or the **Medical Practitioners Award**. These awards have higher minimum rates than the national minimum. The Fair Work Commission publishes the Modern Awards Pay Database with exact classification rates. Always check your award classification – a sonographer or radiographer may have a different rate than a nuclear medicine technologist.

### Tax and Super on Your Medical Imaging Salary

Once you have your annual gross (hourly × 38 × 52), you can estimate **tax** using the 2026–27 resident rates: nil up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% to $135,000; 37% to $190,000; 45% above. Add **Medicare levy** of 2% (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). **Super guarantee** is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. For example, if your annual gross is $120,000, super is $14,400 extra.

### Using the Timesheet and Reference Tables

To quickly convert your hourly rate, use [the timesheet](/). It lets you type a base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. Never type a rate that already includes loading – check the box instead. For more detail, see [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data) for award rates. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page compares your salary to ABS averages.

### Important Notes

This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Medical Imaging Salary: Putting It Together

For a medical imaging professional earning $60 per hour (median hourly from the $2,360 weekly / 38 hours = $62.11, but use your actual rate):
- Weekly: $60 × 38 = $2,280
- Fortnightly: $2,280 × 2 = $4,560
- Annual: $2,280 × 52 = $118,560
- Super (12%): $14,227.20 on top
- Tax (estimate): depends on your total income, but roughly $30,000–$35,000 plus Medicare.

Check your award for minimum rates – they may be higher than the national minimum. Use [job pay](/topics/job-pay) to see typical rates for your role. Remember, casual loading (25%) is added on top of the base hourly rate, not included in it.
